Mobile payments have become ubiquitous as more and more consumers feel comfortable with the new payment service. The global mobile payment market is projected to soar and reach a value of over $8.94 trillion by 2027, which is nearly seven times higher than that in 2019. [[1]] They start to provide a variety of mobile payments to cater to consumers’ needs.
Mobile payments, also known as mobile wallets or mobile money, refers to the payment services provided by banks or other financial institutions and performed via mobile devices. [[2]] Unlike such in-store payments, remote payments take place when consumers transfer money or pay for their merchandise online with any use of electronic devices. Two of the most common mobile wallets in Taiwan are Apple Pay and LINE Pay. Mobile wallets are virtual wallets which enable users to store credit card or bank card information in an app installed on a mobile device. Scanning or tapping their cellphones, users can securely and quickly make the payment within a few seconds. There is no need to bring their wallets or credit cards. [[3]]
However, mobile payments also come with some challenges and risks. In 2021, the torrential rain gave rise to unprecedented flooding in Zhengzhou, one of highly digitalized cities in China, which revealed the risks of mobile payments. Heavily relying on the use of network and mobile devices, residents in Zhengzhou experienced a so-called “digital dark age.” [[4]] This disaster is not only a matter of life and death but an acute reminder of further prevention of possible problems mobile payments may cause.

options_bank.A: For example, consumers can make mobile payments instead of paying in cash or by credit cards in a physical store.
options_bank.B: All they need is a smartphone loaded with mobile wallet apps.
options_bank.C: With the rapid growth of mobile payments, retailers or e-commerce operators are more willing to embrace this change.
options_bank.D: People failed to pay for necessities and lost connection to others due to power and telecom failure.
